# cato_always_on_rule (Resource)

The cato_always_on_rule resource manages an Always On policy rule in the Cato platform. Changes are saved to the draft policy without publishing. Changing at moves the rule; omitting at preserves its current position.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Changes are saved to the draft policy without publishing.
# Changing at moves the rule. Omit at to preserve its current position on updates.

terraform {
  required_providers {
    cato = {
      source = "catonetworks/cato"
    }
  }
}

variable "token" {
  description = "Cato API token (set with TF_VAR_token)."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
}

variable "account_id" {
  description = "Cato account ID (set with TF_VAR_account_id)."
  type        = string
}

variable "baseurl" {
  description = "Cato GraphQL API endpoint."
  type        = string
  default     = "https://api.catonetworks.com/api/v1/graphql2"
}

provider "cato" {
  baseurl    = var.baseurl
  token      = var.token
  account_id = var.account_id
}

resource "cato_always_on_rule" "example" {
  # at = {
  #   position = "LAST_IN_POLICY"
  #   ref      = "section-or-rule-id" # Required for positions relative to a section or rule.
  # }

  rule = {
    name              = "Example Always On rule"
    description       = "Enforce Always On for Windows and macOS devices"
    enabled           = true
    action            = "ENFORCE"
    allow_fail_open   = false
    allow_user_bypass = true
    anti_tamper_mode  = "OFF"

    bypass_duration = {
      time = 30
      unit = "MINUTES"
    }

    platform = ["WINDOWS", "MACOS"]

    # Supply either id or name for each reference. Empty sets match all entities.
    device_posture_profile = [
      # { name = "Managed devices" }, # Alternatively: { id = "device-profile-id" }
    ]
    source = {
      user = [
        # { name = "alice@example.com" }, # Alternatively: { id = "user-id" }
      ]
      users_group = [
        # { name = "Employees" }, # Alternatively: { id = "user-group-id" }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `rule` (Attributes) Parameters for the Always On policy rule (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule))

### Optional

- `at` (Attributes) Position of the new rule in the policy (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--at))

<a id="nestedatt--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `action` (String) Action applied when the rule matches (ENFORCE or IGNORE; API default is ENFORCE)
- `allow_fail_open` (Boolean) Allow direct internet access until a connection to the PoP is established (API default is false)
- `allow_user_bypass` (Boolean) Allow users to bypass Always On (API default is false)
- `anti_tamper_mode` (String) Level of protection against tampering (OFF, MONITOR, or PROTECT; API default is OFF)
- `bypass_duration` (Attributes) Duration of the disconnection allowed when bypassing Always On (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule--bypass_duration))
- `description` (String) Rule description (API default is an empty string)
- `device_posture_profile` (Attributes Set) Device posture profiles matched with logical OR; combined with other criteria using logical AND (API default is an empty collection) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule--device_posture_profile))
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is enabled
- `name` (String) Rule name
- `platform` (Set of String) Operating systems matched with logical OR (ANDROID, CHROMEOS, EMBEDDED, IOS, LINUX, MACOS, or WINDOWS); combined with other criteria using logical AND (API default is an empty collection)
- `source` (Attributes) Source users and user groups matched with logical OR within each criterion and logical AND between criteria (API default contains empty user and users_group collections) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule--source))

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Always On policy rule ID
- `index` (Number) Position or priority of the rule in the policy
- `section` (Attributes) Policy section containing the rule (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule--section))

<a id="nestedatt--rule--bypass_duration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule.bypass_duration`

Required:

- `time` (Number) Bypass duration value
- `unit` (String) Bypass duration unit (HOURS or MINUTES; API default is MINUTES)


<a id="nestedatt--rule--device_posture_profile"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule.device_posture_profile`

Optional:

- `id` (String) Device posture profile ID
- `name` (String) Device posture profile name


<a id="nestedatt--rule--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule.source`

Required:

- `user` (Attributes Set) Individual users defined for the account (API default is an empty collection) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule--source--user))
- `users_group` (Attributes Set) User groups defined for the account (API default is an empty collection) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule--source--users_group))

<a id="nestedatt--rule--source--user"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule.source.user`

Optional:

- `id` (String) User ID
- `name` (String) User name


<a id="nestedatt--rule--source--users_group"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule.source.users_group`

Optional:

- `id` (String) User group ID
- `name` (String) User group name



<a id="nestedatt--rule--section"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule.section`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Policy section ID
- `name` (String) Policy section name



<a id="nestedatt--at"></a>
### Nested Schema for `at`

Required:

- `position` (String) Insertion position (AFTER_RULE, BEFORE_RULE, FIRST_IN_POLICY, FIRST_IN_SECTION, LAST_IN_POLICY, or LAST_IN_SECTION)

Optional:

- `ref` (String) ID of the rule or section relative to which the new rule is positioned
